change: Whole-buffer and range consumers use owner-defined bulk data operations; the per-byte Protocol::read_bytes helper and handwritten whole-buffer byte loops are removed.

contract.delivery: The provider snapshots the requested range, then sends byte values in batches of at most 8192 Oops through the recipient appendByteValues operation.
contract.consumer_lifetime: Each native consumer owns its output Vec and scoped recipient identity. Nested reads are distinct; callbacks after completion fail. No mutable owner borrow spans a callback.
validation: Every delivered value is an immediate byte in 0..255.
Exact promised length is required; overflow, underfill and ignored receiver failure reject the read.
Provider failure propagates with cleanup and error rooting.
Read limits are checked before copying.
Current bulk-operation replacement remains observable; indexed access replacement no longer defines whole-buffer conversion.
contract.other_bulk_operation: Bytes matchesByteValues compares a whole argument group; generated code factories use it for checksum comparison.
contract.unchanged: Id message ABI and direct dispatch, object-payload opacity, code ownership, stackless execution and callback boundaries. The bootstrap data owners gain the bulk data operation; generic Id does not gain an application protocol.

microbenchmark.scope: Old per-byte reference algorithm versus the new reader, using the same native floor and Bytes providers. Alternating order, six samples per mode and size; outputs checked. GC and receiver preparation outside timers.

validation: Core Oop checks passed, including constructor purity, direct dispatch, GC, callbacks and independent C caller.
New bulk tests passed at 0, 1, 8192, 8193 and 1048576 bytes; no indexed byte accessor calls.
Bulk tests cover nested reads, GC, malformed bytes, underfill, overflow, ignored destination failures, expired sinks, and mutation/reallocation of the producer during delivery.
Byte ABI, external-allocation accounting, native values, native incoming conversions, construction purity and String/Error tests passed.
Image roundtrip passed with mapped loading, rebuild and stripped-code cases. The retained image-resave test also passed.
Complete candidate and clean local installation succeeded, including bootstrap/tools image creation and startup checks.
compatibility: Custom byte providers implement the new bulk operation. There is no scalar fallback.
Existing indexed methods remain for indexed reads and general Oop collections/capture arrays.
The executable facade declares its receiving callback once through existing TCC facilities; native module consumers declare theirs in module metadata. No callbacks are compiled per transfer.
remaining_ownership_limits: Cross-owner copying now works in bulk without relaxing opacity.

Directly borrowing another owner's native byte pointer or sharing mutable native storage remains outside the current contract. This implementation performs owned copies and Oop batch encoding rather than zero-copy native views.
limits: Startup figures are fresh processes with warm filesystem caches, serial ABBA, and the same trivial source program. They include source evaluation and process exit.
Microbenchmark gains are specific to transfer size and do not imply that all byte operations become 45-56 times faster.
The local installation is updated from the fix commit; the published v0.19.0 GitHub archive remains immutable and predates this fix.
validation_note: The first image run exposed late facade callback preparation after compilation had been disabled; preparation was moved earlier, and image roundtrip was rerun successfully. The original combined log retains that earlier failure alongside the successful resave test.
